topK.title: Results to Retrieve (top-K)
topK.body:
How many document chunks are added to the AI prompt alongside your question.

• 3 chunks — shortest prompt, fastest answer
• 5 chunks — good balance ✓ default
• 10 chunks — better coverage for multi-part questions
• 15–20 — large documents with scattered information

More chunks mean a longer prompt: more tokens and slightly slower answers.

searchMode.title: Search Mode
searchMode.body:
How relevant chunks are found:

• Hybrid (recommended) — vector and keyword results fused by rank (RRF). Handles both vague questions and exact names, codes and numbers.

• Semantic Only — vector similarity only. Good for paraphrased questions; exact terms may be missed.

• Keyword Only — full-text matching, no embedding call per question. Fastest; fails on paraphrasing.

Chinese works in all three: keywords are matched on overlapping two-character pieces. When vectors can't be used (no embedding service, rebuild needed, service unreachable) every mode falls back to keywords.

chunkSize.title: Chunk Size (tokens)
chunkSize.body:
How many tokens each indexed piece of a document holds (Chinese counts about one token per character).

• Small (128–256) — precise retrieval, more chunks
• Medium (512) — good balance ✓ default
• Large (1024–2048) — more context per chunk, fewer chunks; details can get buried

Smaller chunks mean more embedding requests when indexing.

⚠ Needs an index rebuild after changing.

chunkOverlap.title: Chunk Overlap (tokens)
chunkOverlap.body:
How many tokens adjacent chunks share, so a sentence at a boundary isn't cut in half.

• 0 — no overlap
• 32–64 — recommended ✓ default (64)
• 128–256 — more continuity for narrative text, larger index

⚠ Needs an index rebuild after changing.

minCosine.title: Minimum similarity
minCosine.body:
Vector hits whose cosine similarity is below this value are dropped before ranking. Off by default: similarity scales differ a lot between models (0.3 is a strong match for some and noise for others).

Keyword hits are never filtered by it.

semanticWeight.title: Semantic Weight (Hybrid mode)
semanticWeight.body:
In Hybrid mode, the balance between vector and keyword results when their ranks are fused (RRF).

score = w / (60 + vector rank) + (1 − w) / (60 + keyword rank)

• 0.3 — favor exact terms (names, IDs)
• 0.7 — favor meaning ✓ default
• 1.0 — vectors only
• 0.0 — keywords only

No effect in the other modes.

meetingNote: During meetings: The live transcript is sent as a rolling context window (configured in General settings), not stored in the RAG index. RAG retrieves the top-{{topK}} relevant chunks from your pre-indexed documents. Both are injected into the LLM prompt together.

gemini.title: Gemini Context Cache
gemini.description: Upload your context documents to Gemini's servers once. Each query skips local embedding entirely — ~3-5s faster per response on CPU-only machines.

embedding.title: Embedding service
embedding.description: Turns document chunks and questions into vectors. Use any OpenAI-compatible /embeddings endpoint, or Ollama.

preset.label: Template
preset.hint: Fills in the address and model suggestions; everything stays editable.

provider.label: API style
provider.ollamaV1Warning: This address ends with /v1, which is Ollama's OpenAI-compatible API. Switch the API style to OpenAI-compatible, or remove /v1 and use the Ollama host.

connection.label: Connection
connection.hint: Reuse an LLM connection's address, key and headers.
connection.gone: The LLM connection reused here no longer exists. Save to use the address and key below instead.

dimensions.label: Dimensions
dimensions.hint: Leave empty to use what the model returns. A value here is checked against every response.
dimensions.sendHint: Only for models that can shorten their vectors (OpenAI text-embedding-3, DashScope v3/v4, Zhipu embedding-3…). Other services may reject the request.

advanced.batchSizeHint: Batch size: chunks per request (halved automatically when the service says it is too large). Parallel requests are lowered during meetings. Longer inputs than the limit are cut before sending.
advanced.prefixesHint: Some models expect an instruction in front of the text (nomic, e5, bge-zh, Qwen3-Embedding). Changing the document prefix needs an index rebuild.
advanced.extraHint: Merged into the request body, e.g. Jina's {"task": "retrieval.passage"}. model and input can't be changed here. Changing the document fields needs an index rebuild.
advanced.queryTimeoutHint: Past this the question is answered with keyword search only.

confirm.privacy: Document text will be sent to {{host}} to be embedded.
confirm.rebuild_one: This change produces different vectors: searches use keywords only until you rebuild the index ({{count}} chunk to embed again).
confirm.rebuild_other: This change produces different vectors: searches use keywords only until you rebuild the index ({{count}} chunks to embed again).

test.dimsIgnored: The service ignored the dimensions field and returned {{dims}}-d vectors.
test.addV1: The same address with /v1 at the end answers.

rerank.title: Reranking
rerank.description: An optional second pass: the best fused results go to a rerank model, which orders them by how well they answer the question. If it fails or takes too long, the fusion order is kept and answers go on as usual.
rerank.enabledHint: Each search sends up to {{count}} retrieved chunks and the question to the rerank service.
rerank.incomplete: Set a Base URL (or pick a connection) and a model: until then searches keep the fusion order.

connection.label: Connection
connection.hint: Reuse an OpenAI-compatible LLM connection's address, key and headers. Requests go to its Base URL + /rerank.
connection.gone: The LLM connection reused here no longer exists. Save to use the address and key below instead.

model.label: Model
model.teiHint: TEI serves a single model: the name can stay empty.

format.label: Request format
format.hint: Generic sends {model, query, documents, top_n}: Jina, Cohere, SiliconFlow, Xinference, vLLM, LocalAI and most hosted services. TEI sends {query, texts}: Hugging Face Text Embeddings Inference.

candidates.label: Candidates
candidates.hint: Fused results sent to the reranker (never fewer than the results returned). More can surface better passages but take longer.

timeout.label: Timeout (ms)
timeout.hint: Past this the fusion order is used. 1000–3000 ms suits meetings.

confirm.privacy: Retrieved document chunks and your questions will be sent to {{host}} for reranking.

test.rankedCorrectly: The relevant test passage came out on top.
test.rankedWrong: The relevant test passage did not come out on top: check the model and the request format.
test.slow: This took {{ms}} ms, longer than the {{timeout}} ms timeout: searches would keep the fusion order.

completeness.title: Answer completeness
completeness.subtitle: Return whole paragraphs instead of fragments, and find passages that put things in other words.

expansion.label: Expand results to their context
expansion.hint: Each result brings its neighbouring chunks, or its whole section when that is short enough. Results that meet in a document are merged into one passage. No extra LLM calls; the answer prompt gets longer.
expansion.limitsHint: Past the context limit, later results come back unexpanded.

headings.label: Split at headings
headings.hint: Chunks stay inside one section and carry its heading path (“Chapter 3 › 3.2 Data sources”), which search matches and the model sees. Reads Markdown headings, Word heading styles, PDF bookmarks and numbered headings such as “第一章” or “3.2”. Changing it needs an index rebuild.

rewrite.label: Query rewriting (multi-query)
rewrite.hint: Before each search an LLM writes a few other phrasings of the question; all are searched and the results fused, so passages worded differently are found too. One LLM call per search, routed in LLM settings → Task routing (“Knowledge base query rewriting”). When it fails or runs out of time, the question is searched alone.

summaries.label: Chapter summaries
summaries.hint: While indexing, an LLM writes one summary per chapter, searched along with the text: this helps with questions about a whole chapter. One LLM call per chapter (“Knowledge base chapter summaries” in Task routing); unchanged chapters keep their summary. Turning it on or off needs an index rebuild.
